messages:
maya: Heads up — saw a ~3.8% bump in 5xx across hosted API starting ~12:08 UTC when the canary rolled. Multiple customer tickets about timeouts and gateway errors.

alex: Are errors scoped to particular routes or models?

maya: Mostly /v1/generate and /v1/chat for model rw1-small. Mix of 502 and 504, plus a few token-parse auth failures in support logs.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout triggered by @jordan at 12:05 UTC: raptor-routing v2 -> 10% traffic.

sam: Pushed a small config tweak to the canary: `feature.routing.normalize_headers = true` and adjusted route weights for serp. Canary-only.

alex: normalize_headers could affect how the auth proxy aggregates long Authorization headers. Can we get the exact diff?

sam: Diff snippet:
```
- normalize_headers: false
+ normalize_headers: true
- route_weights.serp: 0.9
+ route_weights.serp: 0.5
```

jordan: Support thread indicates token truncation for some customers — they send very long JWTs in `Authorization` (multi-chunk). normalize_headers logic might be collapsing fragments.

maya: Repro from support (shortened token):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <very-long-token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Result: intermittently 502 / gateway timeout (~10s) for affected requests.

li: Edge logs show increased upstream resets: `upstream prematurely closed connection` and connection timeouts to auth-proxy pool.

ops-oncall: @sam @jordan if header normalization changed bytes sent upstream, we've got a protocol mismatch. Recommend immediate rollback of the canary, open a staging repro, and then retest.

deploy-bot: Rolling back canary: reducing raptor-routing traffic -> 0%. Rollback started 12:21 UTC.

support-bot: Creating incident INC-2026-214 and notifying affected customers / support queue.

maya: After rollback, 5xx dropped from ~3.8% -> ~0.6% within 2 minutes. Gateway errors tailing off.

alex: Next actions: add integration test for long `Authorization` headers, add canary gating check that verifies header passthrough to upstreams, and include header-length smoke in rollout checklist.

sam: I'll revert the normalization change and open a PR with safer normalization plus unit/integration tests. Will validate in staging with long-header stress.

jordan: Thanks all. Who owns the customer update in #support-ops? :thumbsup:

support-bot: Assigned to @maya.

maya: On it — drafting update and scheduling a controlled re-rollout with tests disabled by default.

alex: Add to the postmortem: clarify how config flags interact with proxy expectations and include a runbook entry for this header-normalization class of regressions.

sam: noted, will include that in the PR description and link to the runbook entry.

(ops): closing loop — rollback stable, monitoring continues.
